name: Budget documents: where the C4ISR software money actually sits (FY2026 and FY2027)
summary: The FY2027 President's Budget (released 21 April 2026, now hosted at comptroller.war.gov after the September 2025 'Department of War' rebrand) shows C4ISR software money concentrating in a handful of large, deliberately flexible lines rather than dozens of legacy program elements. The Army's Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2) portfolio is the single largest identifiable C2-software pot: ~$3.78B requested for FY27 across RDT&E and procurement (C2 applications $488.4M RDT&E; C2 data $306.1M; C2 infrastructure ~$1.36B; C2 transport ~$1.36B), up ~28% from the ~$3B provided in FY26, with legacy tactical-network lines (ITN, CPCE/Mission Command, C2 Fix) being divested or folded in. Congress is pushing back on the flexible-funding construct: the FY26 NDAA caps NGC2 obligations at 50% pending a detailed report, and the HASC FY27 chairman's mark cuts $710M. The Department of the Air Force's ABMS/DAF Battle Network RDT&E request was $1,040.5M in FY26 (CBC2 sits inside ABMS under C3BM software and applications); the Navy's CANES procurement/RDT&E was $534.3M in FY26 while Project Overmatch's unclassified 'core' line was only $139.8M in FY25 with most funding classified; the Space Force's FY27 request nearly doubles to $71.3B ($38.4B RDT&E) including a new $1.5B 'Automate Sat C2' program. At the joint level, the FY27 request seeks more than $2B in FY27 (and ~$2.3B across the FYDP) to expand Maven Smart System and the Joint Fires Network for combatant commands, explicitly to move beyond 'fragmented' CJADC2 deployments, while DISA's FY27 O&M books fund Thunderdome zero-trust access to the Secret fabric and a hybrid-cloud Coalition Information Environment / Mission Partner Environment. The 2025 reconciliation law (P.L. 119-21, Title II, ~$150-156B) contains no discrete JADC2/C2-software line; its C2-relevant money flows indirectly via Golden Dome, Indo-Pacific, and 'low-cost weapons/innovation' sections, and DoD planned to obligate essentially all of it in one year. Structurally, the March 2025 software-acquisition memo (Software Acquisition Pathway preferred; CSO/OTA default) and the November 2025 'Warfighting Acquisition System' memo (Portfolio Acquisition Executives replacing PEOs within two years; commercial-first) plus the FY26 NDAA's portfolio-acquisition reforms are what determine how a startup can actually touch this money. Several requested line-level items (TITAN, EWPMT, Rainmaker, Army PNT, DAF DCGS, USMC NOTM, SDA BMC3, CDAO PE-level, DIU FY26/27, contested logistics) could not be verified at PE/dollar level within this session's tool budget and are marked 'Public evidence insufficient' rather than estimated.

findings.title: FY2027 President's Budget released 21 April 2026; justification books now at comptroller.war.gov
findings.detail: The FY2027 request was released on 21 April 2026. Following the September 2025 executive rebrand to 'Department of War', the Comptroller's budget materials (R-1, O-1, RDT&E/Procurement/O&M J-books, Overview Book) are hosted at comptroller.war.gov (comptroller.defense.gov URLs still resolve for older years). Service J-books are at asafm.army.mil (Army), saffm.hq.af.mil / af.mil (DAF), secnav.navy.mil/fmc/fmb (Navy/USMC). The FY2026 R-1 was dated June 2025 (late release).
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: Janes: the NGC2 and C2NOW funding line items were part of the Army's overall USD252.8 billion FY2027 request ... according to the proposal released on 21 April.
findings.source_title: War Budget Materials - FY2027 (Comptroller) / Janes FY27 Army NGC2 article
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Founders can read program-level narrative and out-year (FYDP) funding directly from the J-books; the FY27 books are the current authoritative statement of what the services intend to buy in C2 software.

findings.title: Army NGC2 FY27 request ~$3.78B across RDT&E and procurement, split into four flexible sub-lines
findings.detail: For FY27 the Army requested ~$3.78B for NGC2 plus associated network divestment: $488.4M RDT&E for C2 applications; $306.1M (procurement + RDT&E) for C2 data; ~$1.36B (RDT&E + procurement) for C2 infrastructure; ~$1.36B (RDT&E + procurement) for C2 transport. This is request, not appropriation. The lines are structured as broad portfolio/flexible-funding lines rather than legacy PEs; specific PE numbers for each sub-line were not captured this session (Army RDT&E Vol 3, BA 5A and 5D J-books on asafm.army.mil are the primary source).
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: Breaking Defense: The Army requested $3.78 billion across procurement and RDT&E for NGC2 and its network divestment efforts ... $488.4 million through RDT&E for C2 applications; $306.1 million ... for C2 data; $1.36 billion ... for C2 infrastructure; and $1.36 billion ... for C2 transport.
findings.source_title: Army unveils sweeping XM30 push, $4B bet on NGC2 in newly released budget materials - Breaking Defense
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: The 'C2 applications' ($488.4M) and 'C2 data' ($306.1M) sub-lines are the most software-native and most accessible to small vendors via the NGC2 integrator teams; transport/infrastructure money is dominated by radios, servers and integration.

findings.title: NGC2 trend: ~$3B FY26 request/provided -> ~$3.78B FY27 request (+28%)
findings.detail: DefenseScoop reported in July 2025 that the Army planned roughly $3B for NGC2 in its FY26 request. ExecutiveGov's FY27 guide states the FY27 $3.8B is a 28% increase over the $3B 'provided' in FY26, implying FY26 appropriations were enacted at roughly the requested level for NGC2 (the exact FY26 enacted NGC2 figure and the appropriations act date were not verified this session). FY25 comparison is not apples-to-apples because NGC2 lines did not exist in that form in FY25.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: ExecutiveGov: the Army seeks $3.8 billion across procurement and RDT&E for NGC2 ... a 28 percent increase from the $3 billion provided in FY 2026.
findings.source_title: Army plans to spend roughly $3B on next-gen command and control in fiscal 2026 | DefenseScoop; A Comprehensive Guide to the Army's FY 2027 Budget Request | ExecutiveGov
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: NGC2 is one of very few C2 software lines with a rising two-year trend; it is the Army's stated top modernization priority, which matters more than any IDIQ ceiling.

findings.title: HASC FY27 chairman's mark would cut NGC2 authorization by $710M, signalling discomfort with flexible funding
findings.detail: InsideDefense reported the House Armed Services Committee chairman's mark of the FY27 NDAA would reduce authorized NGC2 funds by $710M, described as the latest sign lawmakers are not fully on board with the Army's NGC2 flexible-funding strategy. SASC mark and final conference outcome for FY27 were not verified this session (FY27 NDAA not enacted as of 24 Sept 2026 per available evidence).
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: The House Armed Services Committee would reduce authorized Next Generation Command and Control funds by $710 million under the newly released chairman's mark of the fiscal year 2027 defense policy bill.
findings.source_title: House defense policy bill would see $700 million drop in authorized NGC2 dollars | InsideDefense
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Budget risk is real: a startup depending on NGC2 flow-down should expect year-to-year volatility and reporting-driven obligation delays.

findings.title: FY26 NDAA caps Army at 50% obligation of NGC2 portfolio funds until a comprehensive report is delivered
findings.detail: The enacted FY26 NDAA (signed December 2025) restricts the Army from obligating more than 50% of NGC2 portfolio funding until it submits a report to the defense committees covering funding plans for existing and new tactical-network experimentation/fielding, a cost-and-capability assessment of current vs proposed solutions, resiliency requirements, and use of NSA-approved high-assurance encryption. Federal News Network also reported Army leaders warning industry not to 'bring negativity' to Congress.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: The final version of the fiscal 2026 defense policy bill caps the Army's ability to obligate more than 50% of its funding for the NGC2 portfolio until the service submits a comprehensive report.
findings.source_title: Lawmakers cap NGC2 funding, Army warns industry not to 'bring negativity' to Congress | Federal News Network
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Signals two hard requirements for anyone building into NGC2: NSA-approved crypto integration and demonstrable resiliency in DDIL conditions; also that cash flow to vendors can be gated by congressional reporting.

findings.title: NGC2 execution status 2025-2026: prototypes with 4th ID / 25th ID, Anduril leads common data layer baseline, I Corps operational fielding
findings.detail: Army awarded an Anduril-led team an OTA prototype for NGC2 with 4th Infantry Division in July 2025 (~$99.6M, RECALL - not re-verified this session) and a Lockheed Martin-led team for 25th ID later in 2025 (RECALL). In June 2026 the Army picked Anduril to lead the NGC2 common data layer baseline (Breaking Defense). In September 2026 Breaking Defense reported the Army readying operational NGC2 technology for I Corps, 'beyond prototypes'; Army leaders described NGC2 as 'ready to scale' (army.mil). Prototype awards are not production programs.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: Breaking Defense (Sept 2026): Beyond prototypes: Army readies operational NGC2 tech for I Corps.
findings.source_title: Beyond prototypes: Army readies operational NGC2 tech for I Corps - Breaking Defense; Army picks Anduril to lead Next Gen C2 common data layer baseline
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: The money in E05-F2 is being executed through integrator-led teams (Anduril, Lockheed) on OTAs; the practical on-ramp for a two-person startup is as a niche app/data-service member of those teams or via the Army's follow-on 'C2 applications' solicitations.

findings.title: Army legacy tactical network / mission command lines (ITN, CPCE, C2 Fix, Unified Network) are being divested or absorbed into NGC2; PE-level FY27 figures not verified
findings.detail: Breaking Defense characterizes the FY27 NGC2 request as covering 'NGC2 and its network divestment efforts'. C2 Fix is a bridging effort to fix the current network while NGC2 is a new architecture. The Army's April 2025 Transformation Initiative (RECALL: SecDef memo 'Army Transformation and Acquisition Reform', 30 April 2025) directed cancellation/consolidation of legacy programs. Specific FY25 enacted / FY26 / FY27 dollar figures for ITN, CPCE (Command Post Computing Environment), Unified Network Operations, and JBC-P/Mounted Mission Command PEs were not verified this session. Public evidence insufficient at PE level.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: NGC2 differs from C2 Fix, another Army network initiative; NGC2 is a whole new architecture whereas C2 Fix is designed to revitalize the Army's current network infrastructure.
findings.source_title: C2 Fix coverage - Breaking Defense; Army FY2027 RDT&E Vol 3 BA 5D J-book
findings.label: INFERENCE
findings.startup_relevance: Building against legacy CPCE/ITN interfaces is a shrinking market; the growth is in NGC2's data layer and application ecosystem.

findings.title: TITAN (Tactical Intelligence Targeting Access Node): prototype under Palantir; FY27 budget line not verified
findings.detail: TITAN is the Army's AI-enabled tactical ground station processing space and terrestrial sensor data, described as a foundational element of Army intelligence modernization. RECALL (not re-verified): Army awarded Palantir a ~$178.4M OTA in March 2024 for 10 TITAN prototypes. The FY27 RDT&E/OPA amounts and PE/line item for TITAN were not captured this session. Public evidence insufficient for FY25 enacted / FY26 / FY27 dollar values.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: TITAN, a tactical ground station that can process data across space and land-based sensors using artificial intelligence, is one of the foundational elements from the intelligence modernization efforts within the Army.
findings.source_title: A Comprehensive Guide to the Army's FY 2027 Budget Request | ExecutiveGov
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: TITAN is a prime-led (Palantir) system; niche opportunities exist in sensor adapters, PED analytics and edge inference, but through the prime.

findings.title: EWPMT: Army cancelled planned follow-on award in April 2024 and restructured its EMS planning-tool approach
findings.detail: DefenseScoop reported on 18 April 2024 that the Army cancelled a planned award for the Electronic Warfare Planning and Management Tool, and on 30 April 2024 that it altered its approach for the electromagnetic-spectrum planning tool (Raytheon was the incumbent). FY26/FY27 funding line for the successor spectrum-management capability was not verified this session. Public evidence insufficient on the FY27 dollar line.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: Army cancels planned award for electronic warfare management tool (DefenseScoop, 18 Apr 2024); Army alters approach for electromagnetic spectrum planning tool (30 Apr 2024).
findings.source_title: Army cancels planned award for electronic warfare management tool | DefenseScoop
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: A restructured, non-incumbent EMS-planning requirement is a genuine opening for software-first vendors, but the funded path in FY27 is unclear and likely rides inside NGC2 'C2 applications' rather than a standalone PE.

findings.title: Rainmaker (Army data fabric): S&T effort with no discrete budget line found
findings.detail: Project Rainmaker is a C5ISR Center-led effort developing common standards/data fabric so combat networks can share data for targeting and AI training (Breaking Defense, 2020). No FY26/FY27 PE or dollar line labelled 'Rainmaker' was found; its work appears to have fed into the NGC2 'C2 data' sub-line ($306.1M FY27) and the common data layer now led by Anduril (INFERENCE). Public evidence insufficient for a Rainmaker-specific dollar figure.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: A low-key Army project known as Rainmaker is quietly developing common standards to let combat networks share data for everything from targeting smart weapons to training AIs.
findings.source_title: Project Rainmaker: Army Weaves 'Data Fabric' To Link Joint Networks - Breaking Defense
findings.label: INFERENCE
findings.startup_relevance: Data-fabric money is now inside NGC2 'C2 data', not a standalone S&T line a startup could target directly.

findings.title: DAF ABMS RDT&E request $1,040.5M in FY26; CBC2 and TOC-L live inside ABMS under C3BM; DAF Battle Network is the DAF's CJADC2 contribution
findings.detail: CRS R48860 (FY2026 Defense Budget: Funding for Selected Weapon Systems) lists an ABMS RDT&E request of $1,040.5M for FY26. A HigherGov budget profile references over $871M for ABMS (likely FY25 enacted or FY26 enacted; ambiguity not resolved). Within the ABMS portfolio, 'C3BM Software and Applications' includes the Cloud-Based Command and Control (CBC2) effort integrating air-defense data for homeland defense; TOC-L (Tactical Operations Center-Light) is also an ABMS deliverable (RECALL). ABMS PE is 0207179F (RECALL - not re-verified). FY27 ABMS figure not captured this session.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: CRS: The FY2026 defense budget includes an Advanced Battle Management System (ABMS) RDT&E request of $1,040.5 million.
findings.source_title: FY2026 Defense Budget: Funding for Selected Weapon Systems | CRS R48860
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: ABMS is the DAF's ~$1B/yr C2 software-heavy line; CBC2 is deliberately built on a microservices/cloud model with multiple vendors, which is more startup-friendly than monolithic programs.

findings.title: DAF FY27 request: overview and IT/cyber priorities published; ABMS/DCGS FY27 line values not verified
findings.detail: The Department of the Air Force published its FY27 Budget Overview and Space Procurement J-book on af.mil in April 2026, and ExecutiveBiz summarized DAF IT, cybersecurity and modernization priorities for FY27. Specific FY27 dollar values for ABMS, DAF DCGS (Distributed Common Ground System), and DAF Battle Network aggregate were not captured this session. Public evidence insufficient at line level for FY27.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: DAF's IT, Cybersecurity, Modernization Priorities for FY27 (ExecutiveBiz headline).
findings.source_title: FY27 Budget Overview - Department of the Air Force
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Follow-up needed: pull PE 0207179F (ABMS) and DCGS lines from the FY27 DAF RDT&E Vol 3 to confirm trend.

findings.title: Navy CANES: $534.3M FY26 request
findings.detail: HigherGov's budget profile (aggregated from Navy J-books) shows a CANES (Consolidated Afloat Networks and Enterprise Services) FY26 request of $534.3M, primarily OPN procurement with an RDT&E component (RECALL: CANES RDT&E is PE 0303138N - not re-verified). CANES is the afloat network hardware/software backbone on which Overmatch applications ride. FY27 CANES value not captured this session.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: The FY26 defense budget for CANES includes a budget request of $534.3M.
findings.source_title: CANES 2026 Budget | HigherGov
findings.sources_note: Aggregator of Tier-1 J-book data; treat as MEDIUM.
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: CANES is hardware/integration dominated (prime-led); the software opportunity is in applications hosted on CANES, funded elsewhere (Overmatch, NIWC efforts).

findings.title: Project Overmatch unclassified 'core' funding was $139.8M in FY25 ($716.7M across FYDP); most Overmatch funding is classified; FY26/FY27 core values not verified
findings.detail: DefenseScoop (March 2024) reported the Navy's core Overmatch request of $139.8M for FY25 and $716.7M across the five-year plan; the bulk of Overmatch spending is understood to sit in classified/restricted lines. FY26 and FY27 Overmatch figures were not surfaced by this session's searches. The Navy's overall FY27 request is $377.5B (+$70B / +23%). Public evidence insufficient for FY26/FY27 Overmatch dollar values.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: The Department of the Navy's 'core funding' request for Project Overmatch is $139.8 million for fiscal 2025 and $716.7 million across the five-year spending plan.
findings.source_title: Navy plans to spend more than $700M on secretive Project Overmatch across FYDP | DefenseScoop
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Overmatch's opacity and classification make it the hardest CJADC2 pillar for an uncleared, non-U.S.-person-founded startup to enter; the visible money is small.

findings.title: Marine Corps C2 (CAC2S, NOTM) funded in FY27 Procurement Marine Corps J-book; line values not verified
findings.detail: The FY27 Procurement, Marine Corps (PMC) justification book on secnav.navy.mil contains the Common Aviation Command and Control System (CAC2S) line. Networking-On-The-Move (NOTM) is also historically a PMC line (RECALL). Dollar values for FY25 enacted / FY26 / FY27 were not extracted this session. Public evidence insufficient at line level.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: The FY 2027 Budget Estimates Justification Book for Procurement Marine Corps includes information on the Common Aviation Command and Control System (CAC2S).
findings.source_title: Procurement Marine Corps - Justification Book FY2027 - Navy
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: USMC C2 lines are modest and procurement-heavy; better approached through MCWL / NavalX / SBIR than the PMC line.

findings.title: Space Force FY27 request $71.3B (65% RDT&E, $38.4B), roughly +80% year-on-year; new $1.5B 'Automate Sat C2' program
findings.detail: Multiple trade sources (SatNews 6 Aug 2026; Air & Space Forces Magazine; Aerospace CSPS budget brief 17 Aug 2026) report a $71.3B Space Force FY27 request, with $38.4B RDT&E, an ~80% increase. The largest new program is 'Automate Sat C2' at $1.5B in FY27, supporting automated satellite command and control. SDA Tranche Transport/Tracking and BMC3 line values were not captured this session (FY27 Air Force Space Procurement J-book is on af.mil). Public evidence insufficient for SDA/BMC3 line values.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: The Space Force requested a total of $71.3 billion for FY2027, with $38.4 billion (65%) for RDT&E ... 'Automate Sat C2' is the largest new program in the Space Force budget with $1.5 billion requested for fiscal year 2027.
findings.source_title: U.S. Space Force Seeks $71 Billion FY2027 Budget - SatNews; Space Force Poised for 80 Percent Funding Boost in 2027 Budget - Air & Space Forces Magazine
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Automated satellite C2 is a software-heavy new start with no entrenched incumbent baseline; it is a plausible entry for autonomy/scheduling software startups, but classification and Golden Dome linkage raise clearance barriers.

findings.title: Joint CJADC2: FY27 request seeks >$2B in FY27 (and ~$2.3B over the FYDP) to expand Maven Smart System and Joint Fires Network to combatant commands
findings.detail: DefenseScoop (28 May 2026) reported DoD wants more than $2B in FY27 to move beyond 'fragmented' CJADC2 deployments, purchasing C2 technology licenses and engineering support for the combatant commands; the request includes ~$2.3B over five years to expand Maven and a related Joint Fires Network, of which ~$1.5B would expand users' access to Palantir's Maven Smart System. The exact split between FY27 and FYDP figures is ambiguous in the summaries and should be confirmed against the OSD/CDAO RDT&E and O&M J-books.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: DOD wants more than $2B in fiscal 2027 to move beyond 'fragmented' CJADC2 deployments ... $1.5 billion would go to expand defense users' access to Palantir's Maven Smart System.
findings.source_title: DOD wants more than $2B in fiscal 2027 to move beyond 'fragmented' CJADC2 deployments | DefenseScoop
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: This is the clearest statement that joint C2 software money is being spent as enterprise licenses to one platform vendor (Palantir); startups should plan to be Maven/MSS-compatible plug-ins or serve edge/DDIL gaps the enterprise platform does not.

findings.title: Palantir vehicles: MSS ceiling raised to ~$1.3B (May 2025) and Army Enterprise Agreement up to ~$10B/10 years (Aug 2025) - ceilings, not obligations
findings.detail: RECALL - not re-verified this session: In May 2025 DoD raised the Maven Smart System contract ceiling to roughly $1.3B; in August 2025 the Army announced an enterprise agreement with Palantir consolidating ~75 contracts with a ceiling of up to $10B over ten years. These are ceilings/vehicles; obligated amounts are far lower and must be checked on usaspending.gov. Consistent with the FY27 CJADC2 request (E05-F17).
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: RECALL: Army-Palantir enterprise agreement ceiling up to $10B over 10 years, consolidating ~75 separate contracts (Aug 2025).
findings.source_title: Army enterprise agreement / MSS ceiling (recall; confirm on usaspending.gov and army.mil)
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Enterprise-agreement consolidation reduces the number of independent small contracts an Army unit can let for C2 analytics; the ecosystem play is integration with, not against, the enterprise platform.

findings.title: DISA FY27 O&M: Thunderdome zero-trust access to the Secret fabric for combatant commands; Coalition Information Environment hybrid-cloud MPE for C2 at Secret-and-below
findings.detail: The FY27 O&M Volume 1 (Department of War, April 2026) states the budget enables combatant commands to access the Secret fabric with immediate zero-trust protection through DISA's Thunderdome program, and that the Coalition Information Environment (CIE) is establishing a secure, unified hybrid-cloud mission partner environment for both C2 and collaboration at Secret and below with allies. Dollar values for Thunderdome, MPE/CIE, and JWCC in FY27 were not extracted this session; JWCC's ceiling is ~$9B across four CSPs (Dec 2022, RECALL).
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: The Coalition Information Environment (CIE) is establishing a secure, unified hybrid cloud mission partner environment for both Command and Control (C2) and collaboration at the Secret and below levels to foster collaboration with our allies.
findings.source_title: Department of War FY2027 Budget Estimates - O&M Volume 1 Part 1
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: MPE/CIE is an explicitly funded FY27 need with an allied-access angle relevant to a German-Indonesian founding team, but delivery runs through DISA and its large integrators; cross-domain and releasability tooling is the software-shaped niche.

findings.title: OSD/CDAO FY27: Advana funded under OSW O&M increase (audit-driven), CDAO AI workforce and 'AI Rapid Capabilities' funded; PE-level CDAO figures not verified
findings.detail: The FY27 O&M Vol 1 states the Office of the Secretary of War increase includes sustainment of automation and AI technologies, financial-systems modernization, and management of the Advana program to achieve a clean opinion on FY2028 financial statements; it also funds CDAO's AI Workforce Program and Center of Excellence, CDAO cybersecurity and risk-management support, and new AI Rapid Capabilities support from AI Assessment and Assurance. The OSD FY27 RDT&E (RDTE_OSW_PB_2027) and Procurement (PROC_OSD_PB_2027) J-books exist but CDAO PE-level totals were not extracted. Public evidence insufficient for CDAO FY25/FY26/FY27 totals.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: The OSW increase includes sustainment of automation and AI technologies, advances financial systems modernization and retirement projects, and manages the Advana program to ensure achieving a clean opinion on the FY 2028 financial statements.
findings.source_title: Department of War FY2027 Budget Estimates - O&M Volume 1; RDTE_OSW_PB_2027
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Advana's justification is now audit/financial-management, not warfighting C2; CDAO's 'AI assessment and assurance' line is a small, software-shaped opportunity (T&E tooling, model assurance).

findings.title: 2025 reconciliation law (P.L. 119-21, Title II): ~$150B defense ($156.2B FY25 budget authority per CRS), no discrete JADC2/C2-software line; DoD planned to obligate essentially all $152B in one year
findings.detail: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act was signed 4 July 2025. CRS IN12580 describes Title II as providing $156.2B in FY2025 for defense purposes across shipbuilding, integrated air and missile defense (Golden Dome), munitions, low-cost weapons/industrial base, air superiority, nuclear, readiness, Indo-Pacific, and a ~$29.8B multi-purpose tranche covering personnel, IT, facilities and fleet modernization. Searches found no dedicated JADC2 or C2-software appropriation in the law. Federal News Network (Feb 2026) reported DoD planned to spend the entire ~$152B within one year. The FY26 request combined $848.3B base with ~$113.3B of reconciliation for a ~$961.6B total (RECALL).
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: CRS: Title II of the legislation contains funding provisions totaling $156.2 billion in FY2025 for defense purposes ... a total of $29.8 billion for several purposes, including personnel, information technology, facility upgrades, and fleet modernization, but does not allocate the total appropriation.
findings.source_title: Defense Funding in the 2025 Reconciliation Law (H.R. 1; P.L. 119-21, Title II) | CRS IN12580
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Reconciliation money is one-time and hardware/munitions-heavy; the software-relevant slices are indirect (Golden Dome C2, Indo-Pacific C2, innovation/low-cost-weapons scaling) and were being obligated fast through existing vehicles, favoring vendors already on contract.

findings.title: Reconciliation slices most relevant to C2/software: Golden Dome (~$24-25B), Indo-Pacific, and 'low-cost weapons / innovation' (~$16B) sections; Navy RDT&E got ~$3.4B
findings.detail: RECALL - not re-verified: Title II included roughly $24-25B for Golden Dome integrated air and missile defense (which necessarily funds battle-management/C2 software), roughly $16B for scaling low-cost weapons and the defense industrial base including DIU-scaled commercial technology and AI ecosystem items, and an Indo-Pacific section. Verified this session: the Navy's FY26 RDT&E of ~$25.7B was 'bolstered by approximately $3.4B in funding from reconciliation' (CRS R48860 summary). Item-level C2 software allocations within these sections are not published as budget lines. Public evidence insufficient at item level.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: For the Navy and Marine Corps, the FY26 request includes roughly $25.7 billion in research and development funding, bolstered by approximately $3.4 billion in funding from reconciliation.
findings.source_title: Golden Dome: Funding in the 2025 Reconciliation Law | CRS IN12576; FY2026 Defense Budget: Funding for Selected Weapon Systems | CRS R48860
findings.label: INFERENCE
findings.startup_relevance: Golden Dome C2/battle management is the largest new software-adjacent pot, but it is highly classified and prime-dominated; not a realistic first market for an uncleared startup.

findings.title: 6 March 2025 SecDef memo 'Directing Modern Software Acquisition to Maximize Lethality': Software Acquisition Pathway preferred; CSO and OTA default solicitation methods
findings.detail: The memo, effective immediately, directs all DoD components to use the Software Acquisition Pathway (SWP) as the preferred method for software development components of business and weapon systems, to use Commercial Solutions Openings and Other Transaction Authorities as the default solicitation/award avenues, and to use modern iterative methods (DevSecOps). USD(A&S) and the DIU director were given 30 days to submit an implementation plan.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: Hegseth: While commercial industry has rapidly adjusted to a software-defined product reality, DoD has struggled to reframe our acquisition process from a hardware-centric to a software-centric approach.
findings.source_title: Hegseth mandates streamlined software acquisition approach in new memo | Defense News; Hegseth issues edict on DOD software acquisition | DefenseScoop
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: This is the single most startup-favorable policy in the set: CSOs/OTAs allow non-traditional vendors to be awarded without full FAR competition, and OTAs are the vehicle through which NGC2 and most DIU work now flows.

findings.title: 7 November 2025 'Warfighting Acquisition System' memo: Portfolio Acquisition Executives replace PEOs within two years; commercial-first; speed as organizing principle
findings.detail: The Acquisition Transformation Strategy memo ('Transforming the Defense Acquisition System into the Warfighting Acquisition System to Accelerate Fielding of Urgently Needed Capabilities to Our Warriors') restructures acquisition around Portfolio Acquisition Executives with all major acquisition activities transitioning to PAEs within two years, prioritizes speed to capability, and directs maximum use of commercial products, direct-to-supplier relationships and alternative procurement methods. Trade press reported Hegseth telling contractors to adapt or 'fade away'.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: Speed to capability delivery is now our organizing principle. (memo, as quoted by Winston & Strawn / Holland & Knight)
findings.source_title: Hegseth looking to sideline laggards in acquisition community, industry | DefenseScoop; Hegseth unveils 'transformation' of DoD acquisition system | Federal News Network
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Portfolio-level buying (e.g., an Army C2 portfolio executive) concentrates decision authority; startups need one portfolio sponsor rather than many PEO/PM relationships, but portfolio managers will also favor consolidated enterprise vendors.

findings.title: FY26 NDAA (signed December 2025, ~$901B topline) enacts portfolio-based acquisition, raises acquisition thresholds, and overhauls requirements
findings.detail: The FY26 NDAA was signed in December 2025. Law-firm analyses (Crowell, Holland & Knight, Greenberg Traurig, Morgan Lewis) describe it as overhauling the acquisition lifecycle and requirements process toward portfolio-based acquisition with built-in product support, and raising critical acquisition thresholds (simplified acquisition, commercial, OTA-related). The joint explanatory statement is on armedservices.house.gov. Specific section numbers were not verified this session.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: The FY 2026 NDAA overhauls the DOD acquisition lifecycle and requirements process for major systems, shifting to a new portfolio-based acquisition model with product support management built in.
findings.source_title: FY 2026 NDAA: The Substantial Impact ... on Federal Procurement Law | Greenberg Traurig; Trump Signs $901B FY 2026 Defense Authorization Bill Into Law | GovConWire
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Raised thresholds enlarge the pool of small awards that can be made with simplified procedures, which is where a $250k-funded startup's first contracts realistically sit.

findings.title: FY26 appropriations timeline: 43-day shutdown (1 Oct - 12 Nov 2025), CR, then full-year FY26 appropriations enacted before the FY27 request
findings.detail: RECALL (HIGH): the federal government shut down from 1 October to 12 November 2025 before a CR was enacted. INFERENCE: because FY27 materials (Janes, ExecutiveGov) compare against 'FY 2026 appropriated' and 'provided in FY 2026' levels, full-year FY26 defense appropriations were enacted before 21 April 2026; the enactment date and NGC2 enacted line were not verified this session. Fox News reported the Marine Corps warning that a year-long CR would prevent execution of its new counter-drone plan, illustrating CR risk to new-start C2/C-UAS efforts.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: Janes: ... just over a 10% increase from the total FY 2026 appropriated funding levels.
findings.source_title: Pentagon budget 2027: US Army requests over USD3 billion for NGC2, C2NOW | Janes
findings.label: INFERENCE
findings.startup_relevance: Under a CR, new starts and production-rate increases are frozen; a startup's first-year revenue plan should not assume October obligations.

findings.title: Counter-UAS C2: JIATF-401 stood up (Aug 2025) as the DoD-wide C-sUAS lead; Army FY27 request emphasizes C-sUAS; specific C-UAS C2 software line not isolated
findings.detail: JIATF-401 replaced the Joint C-sUAS Office as the Department-wide counter-small-UAS synchronizer (RECALL: established by SecDef memo August 2025); a JIATF-401 Quick Reference Guide was published on media.defense.gov on 8 September 2026. ExecutiveGov's FY27 Army guide headlines C-sUAS alongside NGC2 and M-SHORAD as major FY27 investments. Dollar values for C-UAS C2 software (e.g., FAAD C2 successor, Army 'C-sUAS' lines) were not extracted. Public evidence insufficient at line level.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: JIATF 401's mission is to synchronize the Department's counter-UAS efforts and accelerate the delivery of effective capabilities to protect warfighters and the homeland.
findings.source_title: Joint Interagency Task Force 401 (JIATF-401) 2026 Counter-Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Quick Reference Guide
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: C-UAS C2 is a fast-moving, commercially-solicited area (JIATF-401 runs frequent industry demos) with lower classification barriers at the base-defense tier; the funding is real but spread across services.

findings.title: JADC2/CJADC2 has no single program element; funding is distributed across service programs (NGC2, ABMS, Overmatch, SDA) plus joint CDAO/Joint Staff lines
findings.detail: CRS IF11493 and trade analysis consistently note that JADC2 is a concept/strategy rather than a budget line, and that DepSecDef Hicks declared a CJADC2 'minimum viable capability' delivered in February 2024 (RECALL). The FY27 joint request (E05-F17) is the first time a >$2B joint-level C2 software figure has been explicitly tied to CJADC2 in the request.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: TENET: JADC2: Is It a Program, a Concept, or a Budgetary Black Hole?
findings.source_title: Joint All-Domain Command and Control (JADC2) | CRS IF11493
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Do not build a business plan around 'JADC2 funding'; target a specific service line (NGC2 C2 apps/data, ABMS/CBC2, SDA BMC3) or the CDAO enterprise-licence pool.

findings.title: DIU budget: FY24 enacted roughly $983M (congressional plus-up); FY26/FY27 DIU lines not verified this session
findings.detail: RECALL - not re-verified: Congress boosted DIU to about $983M in FY24 appropriations versus a ~$100M-level request, and DIU has since run larger CSO-based programs (Replicator, etc.). FY26 request and FY27 request for DIU were not surfaced. Public evidence insufficient for FY26/FY27 DIU totals.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: RECALL: FY24 appropriations provided approximately $983M to DIU.
findings.source_title: Defense Innovation Unit (diu.mil) - recall; confirm in FY27 OSD RDT&E J-book
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: DIU CSOs remain the most accessible federal on-ramp for a commercial software startup, and the March 2025 memo made DIU co-author of the software-acquisition implementation plan.

findings.title: Contested logistics C2: no discrete C2-software budget line identified
findings.detail: The Army stood up a Contested Logistics Cross-Functional Team in 2023 (RECALL) and contested logistics appears as a theme in FY26/FY27 narratives, but no PE or line labelled contested-logistics C2 software was surfaced by this session's searches. Public evidence insufficient.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: Public evidence insufficient.
findings.source_title: Not found this session
findings.label: HYPOTHESIS
findings.startup_relevance: Absence of a line is not evidence of opportunity; logistics C2 money is likely inside enterprise business systems and Advana rather than tactical C2.

findings.title: FY27 service toplines: Army $252.8B (+10% vs FY26 appropriated), Navy $377.5B (+23%), Space Force $71.3B (~+80%)
findings.detail: Janes reports the Army's FY27 request at $252.8B, just over 10% above total FY26 appropriated levels. Naval Technology and navy.mil report the Department of the Navy at $377.5B, +$70B / +23%. Space Force $71.3B per SatNews / Air & Space Forces Magazine. The overall DoD FY27 topline was not captured this session (RECALL, MEDIUM: the President signalled a ~$1.5T FY27 defense target in January 2026).
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: The US Department of the Navy submitted a $377.5bn budget request for Fiscal Year 2027, representing a $70bn or 23% increase compared to the previous year.
findings.source_title: US Navy submits record $377.5bn funding request for fiscal 2027 | Naval Technology; Department of the Navy Releases FY27 Budget Request | navy.mil
findings.label: FACT
findings.startup_relevance: Rising toplines increase the number of new starts and OTA prototypes, but Congress's FY27 marks (E05-F4) show the request is not the appropriation.

findings.title: Army PNT (APNT/MAPS/DAPS): budget line not verified this session
findings.detail: Army Assured PNT efforts (Mounted Assured PNT System, Dismounted APNT, PNT Modernization) are funded via Army RDT&E and OPA lines but their FY25 enacted / FY26 / FY27 values were not extracted this session. Public evidence insufficient.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: Public evidence insufficient.
findings.source_title: Army FY2027 RDT&E Vol 3 BA 5A J-book (source to check)
findings.label: HYPOTHESIS
findings.startup_relevance: PNT is hardware/crypto heavy; software-only PNT resilience (e.g., sensor-fusion navigation) has a narrow but real niche, funding path unclear.

findings.title: Startup-relevant synthesis: the accessible C2-software money in FY26-27 sits in (1) NGC2 C2 applications/data sub-lines, (2) ABMS/CBC2 microservices, (3) CDAO enterprise-license and AI-assurance pools, (4) C-UAS C2, all reached via OTA/CSO under the 2025 directives
findings.detail: Combining E05-F2, F11, F17, F19, F23, F24 and F27: roughly $0.8B (NGC2 apps+data) + ~$1B (ABMS) + >$2B (joint CJADC2/Maven licences) + DISA MPE/Thunderdome + emerging C-UAS C2 are the software-native pools; Overmatch, SDA BMC3 and Golden Dome C2 are larger but classified/prime-dominated. The 2025 directives make CSO/OTA the default path, but the FY26 NDAA obligation cap and HASC FY27 cut show that flow-down to small vendors will be lumpy. For a $250k two-founder startup with one non-U.S. person, the realistic FY27 entry points are SBIR/STTR, DIU/JIATF-401 CSOs, and sub-tier participation on NGC2 or CBC2 integrator teams; ITAR/FOCI/clearance implications require specialist legal review.
findings.quote_or_paraphrase: Synthesis of this evidence sweep.
findings.source_title: E05 synthesis
findings.label: INFERENCE
findings.startup_relevance: Direct guidance on which lines a startup can plausibly touch versus which are structurally closed.

saturation_statement: Twelve searches and two blocked fetches were sufficient to establish the FY27 release, the NGC2 portfolio structure and dollar values, the congressional pushback (FY26 NDAA cap, HASC FY27 cut), the FY26 ABMS and CANES lines, Space Force and joint CDAO/CJADC2 FY27 headline figures, DISA FY27 narrative, the reconciliation structure, and the 2025-26 acquisition directives. Not saturated: PE-level FY25 enacted / FY26 enacted / FY27 request values for TITAN, EWPMT, Army PNT, DAF DCGS, USMC CAC2S/NOTM, SDA Transport/BMC3, CDAO, DISA, DIU, C-UAS C2 and contested logistics; the ambiguity between FY27 and FYDP figures in the CJADC2/Maven request; and the FY26 appropriations enactment date. Those require direct reads of the FY27 R-1/P-1 and service J-books (comptroller.war.gov, asafm.army.mil, saffm.hq.af.mil, secnav.navy.mil/fmc/fmb), which the egress proxy blocked this session.
